correctness.rationale: Anchoring the shared hub makes the edge-Lipschitz feasible set an exact product of blade polytopes with all vertices of type 0/1 or 0/(-1). Strict positivity of the centered variance Hessian on anchored functions forces every optimizer to such a vertex. For signed active counts, the exact numerator is NK−S²; sign-flip/fill improvements force each partial optimizer to consist of one partially positive, uniquely largest blade versus fully negative others. Its integer quadratic has center Q+N/2; rounding proves both regimes, the equality cases, and the exact floor-square gap. The uniform-blade formula follows by minimal signed discrepancy; the giant-blade limit is 1/4. Exact independently implemented labelled and active-count enumeration checks specified finite instances without substituting finite experiments for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The original spread paper gives existence/integral structure, random graph work gives stochastic graph-family bounds, and later extremizer studies treat general questions and different examples. None of the inspected relevant source statements entails an all-tuple exact heterogeneously sized vertex-clique-bouquet spread, its partition-discrepancy regime, strict dominant-blade transition, or full optimizer classification. Existing claims on the same graph family address negative type, heat-flow contraction and transport, not this variance optimization. The possible existence of an unindexed equivalent is a stated residual risk.
residual_risks: One-point sums may be treated under other terminology in unavailable or unindexed literature; exhaustive global originality cannot be inferred from unsuccessful queries.
The full proofs of every potential older general result in the literature were not exhaustively reviewed; any stronger directly covering result would supersede an originality assertion.
The optimal fluctuation formula is proved for uniform real-valued vertex observables only, not weighted measures or other moments.

value.rationale: Graph spread is a natural sharp Lipschitz variance and product-metric concentration parameter. For every tuple of positive clique sizes this theorem determines the exact answer and every optimizer, expressing balanced behavior through a nontrivial subset-sum discrepancy and the competing dominant regime through a one-blade integer quadratic. The 3Q+2 structural transition and exact floor-square gain are motivated boundaries of a complete infinite-family classification, not an arbitrary finite computation.
